items.title: Jev Desktop: Jev Inside Codex Computer Use
items.content:
Jev Desktop is the cleanest answer yet to “how do I actually use Jev to drive my computer?” It’s an open-source Codex plugin that drops Jev’s sub-second decision loop inside Codex Computer Use — for browser tabs and native macOS apps — so Codex does the thinking, Jev does the fast clicking, and anything consequential comes back to you. I’ve covered the wider pattern in my Jev computer use guide (and it features in the ecosystem tour above); this page is the specific tool: what it does, the exact install, its safety model, and where it stops.

Key takeaways

- What it is: an MIT-licensed Codex plugin (v0.2.0) adding a bounded Jev decision loop inside Codex Computer Use — browser tabs and native macOS apps.

- The division of labour: Codex plans, prepares text and verifies; Jev picks the operation and target in one request; Computer Use performs the click, fill, scroll or shortcut.

- The safety line: send, publish, payment, deletion, upload, login, installation and permission changes are never executed by Jev’s fast loop — they return to Codex and your authorisation.

- No screenshots: Jev reads Accessibility text, so apps without accessibility info, canvases and custom widgets fall back to normal visual Computer Use.

## What Jev Desktop actually does

Codex Computer Use is powerful and slow in the way all screenshot-driven agents are: look, think, act, repeat. Jev Desktop keeps that runtime and inserts a fast lane. Codex scopes the task and decides whether a quick path applies; if it does, Jev Desktop opens one bounded session in which Computer Use reads accessibility snapshots, the elements are indexed, and Jev — TypeSafe’s decision model — chooses an operation (click, type text, fill a field group, scroll, done, or blocked) and a compatible target in a single request. Only the target matching the chosen operation is validated and allowed to execute.

What it deliberately doesn’t do matters as much: per the README, it installs no second browser controller, calls no private Computer Use APIs, doesn’t need Browser Harness, and doesn’t use a model to generate field text — any text it types comes from values Codex prepared in advance. It’s a judgement layer inside a runtime you already trust, which is the whole Jev agent pattern in miniature.

## Installing Jev Desktop

Requirements: Codex desktop or CLI with plugin support, Node.js 22+, Python 3.10+, and a TypeSafe API key — see my access guide for how to get one. The install, exactly as the README gives it:

- `codex plugin marketplace add yikangy873-gif/jev-desktop`

- `codex plugin add jev-desktop@yikangy873-plugins`

- `cd ~/.codex/plugins/cache/yikangy873-plugins/jev-desktop/*`

- `python3 scripts/setup.py`

- `node scripts/doctor.mjs --live` — the health check

One detail I like: `setup.py` gives you a local loopback URL, and that’s where your TypeSafe key goes — not into the Codex chat. Keys pasted into chats end up in transcripts; this keeps it out. Then just ask Codex naturally: “use Jev Desktop to apply these filters in the current tab and stop when the results load.”

Want this working in your business, not just bookmarked? Wiring fast computer-use agents into your daily workflows safely is exactly the kind of thing we build together inside the AI Profit Boardroom — 3,700+ members, four live calls a week, daily tutorials, plug-and-play templates and a 30-day roadmap so you ship instead of watch.

Prefer it mapped 1-on-1 first? Book a free strategy session and we’ll plan it for your exact situation.

## The Jev Desktop safety model and limits

Jev’s fast loop CAN
Always returns to Codex / you

Click buttons, links, checkboxes, tabs, radios, menu items
Send, publish, payment

Fill fields from Codex-prepared values
Deletion, upload

Fill field groups (with freshness checks)
Login, installation

Scroll allowed regions; use prepared non-submitting shortcuts
Permission changes

That split is exactly right for a computer-use tool: the reflex-speed model handles navigation and form mechanics; anything irreversible or security-relevant goes through the slower, accountable path. The README reports v0.2.0 passes 123 offline automated tests covering operation/target isolation, scoping, stale state, bridge authentication and prepared-value locality.

Honest limits, dated 28 September 2026: speed still depends on app launch and page loading; apps without accessibility data, canvas interfaces and custom widgets need ordinary visual Computer Use; it’s a young community project (v0.2.0, MIT, not a TypeSafe or OpenAI product). The test count is the author’s own — read the code before trusting it with real accounts. Related community builds (jev-computer-use, jev-browser-use) make their own speed claims; treat those as vendor numbers until you’ve timed them yourself.

## The bottom line on Jev Desktop

Jev Desktop is the most carefully designed way to put Jev’s speed into real computer use right now: Codex keeps the brain and the permissions, Jev picks actions from accessibility text in one request, Computer Use does the hands, and every consequential click comes back to you. Five commands to install, key entered outside the chat, and clear limits on what it touches — start with repetitive browser chores and let it earn more.

## FAQ: jev desktop

### What is Jev Desktop?

An open-source (MIT) Codex plugin that adds a bounded Jev decision loop inside Codex Computer Use for browser tabs and native macOS apps: Codex plans and verifies, Jev chooses the action and target, Computer Use executes.

### How do I install Jev Desktop?

With Codex plugin support, Node 22+, Python 3.10+ and a TypeSafe key: add the yikangy873-gif/jev-desktop marketplace, add the jev-desktop plugin, run scripts/setup.py from the plugin cache folder, then node scripts/doctor.mjs –live to check it.

### Is Jev Desktop safe?

Its design is careful: send, publish, payment, deletion, upload, login, installation and permission changes are never run by Jev’s fast loop and go back to Codex for your authorisation. It’s still young community code, so read it before use on important accounts.

### Does Jev Desktop see my screen?

No — Jev reads accessibility text rather than screenshots. Apps without accessibility information, canvases and custom widgets fall back to Codex’s normal visual Computer Use.

### Where do I put my TypeSafe API key?

In the local loopback page that setup.py opens — not in the Codex chat, which keeps the key out of your conversation transcripts.

### Is Jev Desktop an official TypeSafe or OpenAI tool?

No — it’s a community project published on GitHub under the MIT licence, using TypeSafe’s Jev API inside OpenAI’s Codex Computer Use.

items.title: Claude SEO Skill for Claude Code: Build & Install
items.content:
A Claude SEO skill for Claude Code is the difference between asking Claude to “write an SEO article” and having it run your exact SEO process — your research method, your formatting rules, your CTAs, your publishing steps — every time, without re-explaining. I’ve written about the skill I use to rank; this page is the how-to underneath it: what a Claude Code skill actually is, where the files go, a SKILL.md skeleton you can copy, the rules worth putting in it, and why I run several small SEO skills instead of one giant one. The video above shows the Claude Code SEO agent this approach grew out of.

Key takeaways

- A Claude Code skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter ( `name`, `description`) on top, your process in plain markdown below.

- Location decides scope: `~/.claude/skills/` for every project on your machine, or `.claude/skills/` inside one project.

- The description is the trigger — Claude reads it to decide when to load the skill, so write it like a list of the requests it should handle.

- Split by job: I run separate skills for keyword research, SEO articles and WordPress posting — small skills trigger reliably and are easy to fix.

&

## How a Claude SEO skill for Claude Code works

Claude Code skills are packaged instructions that load on demand. Each one lives in its own folder with a `SKILL.md` file; the frontmatter tells Claude what the skill is called and when to use it, and the body holds the actual process. When a request matches the description, Claude pulls the skill in and follows it — or you can call it directly by name. Nothing is compiled or installed: it’s a markdown file, which means your whole SEO method becomes something you can read, version and edit.

That’s why skills beat prompts for SEO. A prompt is whatever you remember to type today; a skill is the process you decided on when you were thinking clearly — the heading rules, the internal-link rules, the source requirements, the CTA placement — applied identically on the hundredth article as on the first.

## Installing a Claude SEO skill for Claude Code

Create the folder and the file (user-level, so it works in every project):

- `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/seo-articles`

- Create `~/.claude/skills/seo-articles/SKILL.md` with frontmatter like this:

- `---` / `name: seo-articles` / `description: Write and publish SEO articles. Use when asked for an SEO article, a ‘best X’ listicle, or to publish a keyword to my sites.` / `---`

- Below the frontmatter, write the process as numbered steps: research, outline rules, writing rules, QA checks, publish and index.

Restart your Claude Code session and ask for an SEO article — it should announce it’s using the skill. If it doesn’t, your description is too vague; add the exact phrases you actually type. For a single site, put the folder in that project’s `.claude/skills/` instead so it only loads there. The Agent OS SEO Pack takes the same approach, shipping a ready-made `blog-post.md` skill file you drop into your home site’s `.claude/skills` folder — covered in my Claude SEO tool guide.

Want this working on your site, not just bookmarked? Getting the exact SEO skill files I use, set up in your Claude Code is exactly what we build together inside the AI Profit Boardroom — 3,700+ members, four live calls a week, daily tutorials, plug-and-play templates and a 30-day roadmap.

Prefer it mapped for your exact site first? Book a free SEO strategy session and we’ll build your gameplan together.

## What to put inside your Claude SEO skill

Section
What it tells Claude
Why it matters for rankings

Source rule
Never write without a real source — transcript, docs, data
Kills generic AI filler; gives the page facts worth citing

Keyword placement
Keyword in the first line, 2+ headings and the last line
Relevance signals, applied every time

Answer-first blocks
Direct answer in the first sentence of each section
Wins snippets and AI answers (AEO)

Internal links
Link to 3+ existing pages; check they exist first
Topical clusters, no broken links

Schema & FAQ
Article + FAQPage JSON-LD, 4–6 FAQs
Parsability for search and answer engines

QA gate
Word count, headings, links, CTAs checked before publish
Consistency at scale

Publish & index
Push live, verify, submit for indexing
Same-day discovery

Keep one job per skill. My own setup runs keyword-research (finds gaps from Search Console), seo-articles (writes and deploys to a static-site network) and wordpress-posts (publishes to WordPress over the REST API) as separate skills. Each has a tight description, so the right one loads for the right request, and when a rule needs changing I edit one file, not a 3,000-word monster.

Honest limits, dated 28 September 2026: a skill is only as good as the rules in it — it encodes your process, it doesn’t invent a better one. Start with a small batch, read every output, and tighten the rules where it drifts. And never put passwords or API keys inside a SKILL.md: skills are plain text, so reference a credentials file the skill reads instead.

## The bottom line on a Claude SEO skill for Claude Code

A Claude SEO skill for Claude Code is a folder, a SKILL.md, a sharp description and your process written down — and it turns Claude from a writer into a teammate who follows your SEO method every time. Build one skill per job, put your ranking rules in plain language, test on a small batch, and refine. Want my exact skill files instead of building from scratch? Members get them inside the AI Profit Boardroom.

## FAQ: claude seo skill for claude code

### What is a Claude SEO skill for Claude Code?

A folder containing a SKILL.md file that tells Claude Code your SEO process — research, writing rules, QA, publishing — with frontmatter describing when to use it. Claude loads it automatically when a request matches.

### Where do Claude Code skills go?

In ~/.claude/skills/ for every project on your machine, or in a project’s.claude/skills/ folder to limit it to that project. Each skill gets its own folder with a SKILL.md inside.

### Why isn’t Claude using my SEO skill?

Usually the description is too vague. Rewrite it to include the exact phrases you use — ‘SEO article’, ‘best X listicle’, ‘publish to my sites’ — then start a new session.

### What rules should an SEO skill include?

A no-source-no-article rule, keyword placement, answer-first sections, verified internal links, Article and FAQPage schema, a pre-publish QA gate, and publish-and-index steps.

### Should I use one big SEO skill or several?

Several small ones. Separate skills for keyword research, article writing and publishing trigger more reliably and are much easier to fix when something drifts.

items.title: Claude SEO Tool: The Agent OS SEO Pipeline
items.content:
The Claude SEO tool I actually use isn’t a SaaS dashboard — it’s the SEO tab inside Agent OS, my local command centre. You drop in a video transcript, type a keyword, and Claude writes a unique post for each of your sites with your videos, CTAs, schema and bio built in, then deploys them all to Netlify. The system behind it is what the video above breaks down — a site I’ve never logged into going from zero to 1,300 clicks a day, and #1 in Google’s AI Overview for “best GEO expert”. Here’s what the tool does, how it’s set up, and where its limits are.

Key takeaways

- What it is: the SEO tab in Agent OS — Claude writes one unique post per site from a single transcript, and one click deploys them to Netlify.

- Each post ships with a different CTR-focused title and opening hook, your video embeds, CTAs back to your offer, schema markup and a bio block.

- Setup takes about 45 minutes: download the SEO Pack, point the config at your sites, drop the `blog-post.md` skill in, add a transcript.

- It runs locally — you own the content, the sites and the traffic. Agent OS and the SEO Pack come with the AI Profit Boardroom.

## What the Claude SEO tool actually does

The workflow is built around one idea: film once, publish everywhere. In the SEO tab you click Generate, type the keyword you want to rank for, pick a slug and choose a transcript. Claude reads your skill file and the transcript and streams out a post for each site — same core substance from your video, but a distinct title and opening per site, with your older videos woven in where they’re relevant. Then Deploy builds each site and pushes it to Netlify; a history view tracks every post.

It works with any static site generator — the guide uses Eleventy, and Astro, Hugo or Next.js work too — because the tool just writes posts into each site’s posts folder and runs the deploy. There’s no hosted platform in the middle and no per-post fee: it’s Claude, your files and your Netlify account.

## Setting up the Claude SEO tool

- 1. Get Agent OS running on your laptop (the Agent OS v2 guide covers it).

- 2. Download the SEO Pack from the SEO tab: `blog-post.md` (the skill), `seoPipeline.ts.template` (site config), an example transcript and a README.

- 3. Set up your sites — each in its own local folder, connected to its own Netlify project.

- 4. Fill in the config: an id, display name, live URL, local path and posts folder for each site.

- 5. Drop the skill in: copy `blog-post.md` into your home site’s `.claude/skills` folder, then edit the brand-voice and video-library sections so posts sound like you and embed your videos.

- 6. Add a transcript to `.claude/transcripts` with a lowercase, hyphenated filename — Agent OS picks it up automatically.

- 7. Generate, then Deploy — posts are typically live across your sites within a few minutes.

If something breaks, the fixes are usually simple: sites not showing means a config path is wrong (restart Agent OS); a failed deploy usually means the Netlify CLI is logged out (`netlify status`, then `netlify login`).

Prefer it mapped for your exact site first? Book a free SEO strategy session and we’ll build your gameplan together.

The tool is the publishing engine; results come from what you feed it. The pieces that matter most, from my own recent videos:

Piece
What I do
Receipt (as shown on camera)

Keywords
Search Console ‘impressions, no clicks’ and striking-distance queries; Google autosuggest for low-competition topics
A site taken from 0 to 474 clicks a day, 50,000+ clicks total (26 Sept video)

Content
Transcript-sourced posts, answer-first, 3–5 low-competition articles a day
93,000 AI mentions and 418 daily clicks from one simple system (27 Sept video)

Authority
E-E-A-T: author persona, about page, branded search, backlink outreach
#1 in Google’s AI Overview for ‘best GEO expert’

Publishing
Claude writes, Netlify deploys, indexing submitted
0 to 1,300 clicks a day on a site I’ve never logged into

Honest expectations, dated 28 September 2026: those numbers are from my own sites, shown in my videos — they’re not a promise of what yours will do. In my experience a new site takes roughly 3–6 months before this kind of system starts paying off, and results depend on keyword choice, niche and authority. The tool makes publishing fast; it doesn’t replace picking winnable keywords or earning links. Keep each site’s post genuinely distinct — unique titles and hooks at minimum — and review before you deploy.

The Claude SEO tool in Agent OS turns one video transcript into unique posts for every site you run, with your videos, CTAs and schema built in, deployed in one click — running on your own machine, with your own sites and traffic.
